risks.note: MD&A flags that constant innovation in AR/VR technology may require frequent upgrades to remain competitive, and that fast-paced innovation may render existing solutions outdated if not upgraded in time.
MD&A states that limited mainstream adoption of AR/VR in certain industries can impact revenue consistency.

MD&A flags an increasing number of startups and global players entering the AR/VR space, which may impact margins, and warns that entry of new domestic and international players with advanced capabilities could erode market share.

MD&A notes that budget constraints during economic downturns may lead clients to defer tech-based investments, and that delayed decision-making or reduced technology budgets can impact project pipelines.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects the AR/VR industry to grow exponentially, supported by falling hardware costs, improved accessibility and innovation in software development.
- Increasing enterprise adoption of AR/VR for training, product visualisation and remote collaboration is cited as a demand driver.
- The Indian market is described as a high-potential landscape for AR/VR adoption due to favourable demographics, rising internet penetration and supportive government initiatives toward digitalisation and Industry 4.0.
- The evolution of Web 3.0 and the metaverse is said to be moving AR/VR beyond niche use …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- MD&A flags that constant innovation in AR/VR technology may require frequent upgrades to remain competitive, and that fast-paced innovation may render existing solutions outdated if not upgraded in time.
- MD&A states that limited mainstream adoption of AR/VR in certain industries can impact revenue consistency.
- MD&A flags an increasing number of startups and global players entering the AR/VR space, which may impact margins, and warns that entry of new domestic and international players with advanced capabilities could erode market share.
- MD&A notes that budget constraints during economic downturns may lead clients to defer tech-based investments, and that delayed decision-making or reduced technology budgets can impact project pipelines.
- MD&A notes immersive solutions often process user data, posing potential privacy and security risks.
- MD&A flags difficulty in acquiring and retaining specialised AR/VR development talent as a threat to execution capacity - acute given the Company reports only 1 permanent employee on roll as at 31 March 2026.
- MD&A notes the absence of universal standards in AR/VR development may hinder integration and scalability of its solutions.
- The report records nil revenue from operations for FY2025-26 against Rs 23.90 lakhs in the prior year, and attributes the collapse in the trade receivables and net capital turnover ratios to the 'absence of revenue from operations during the current year' - a structural going-concern-scale concentration risk for a single-activity, one-employee company.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Remain focused on delivering AR, VR and 360 degree immersive solutions; the report states there was no change in the Company's business operations during FY2025-26.
- Target immersive-technology use cases across education, real estate, tourism, healthcare, manufacturing, retail and entertainment rather than a single vertical.
- Conserve resources for future growth by not declaring a dividend for the year.
